correctness.rationale: A complete 16-bit complementary-feedback-table parametrization covers every binary order-five de Bruijn cycle uniquely after rooting at 00000. A second Euler-tour enumeration produces the same 2048 canonical cycles. Every one of 65536 rooted length-32 words is evaluated by interval LPS dynamic programming and independently by LCS against its reversal; every result agrees. Verified exact frequencies and margins are asserted in standalone checker.py and furnished as summary.json. The finite enumeration exhausts the theorem domain, while no statement is made for larger orders.

value.rationale: The circular longest palindromic subsequence is a studied natural invariant and equals the maximum number of retained symbols under deletion-to-palindrome optimization. The theorem settles a sharp all-cycle guarantee at the first substantial complete binary de Bruijn order (2048 necklaces), and supplies the entire root-sensitive distribution rather than a hand-picked example. In particular it separates the general all-binary-circular length-32 minimum 24 from the de Bruijn-specific 25 and quantifies variance despite identical length-five factor coverage. These are motivated complete finite-class results, not a substitution into a known table.
